questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The nerve most commonly injured in a mid-shaft fracture of the humerus is:
questions.explanation: Radial nerve runs in the radial groove on the posterior humerus and is vulnerable in mid-shaft fractures.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The nerve supplying the deltoid muscle is:
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve supplies deltoid and teres minor and winds around the surgical neck of the humerus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A lesion of the median nerve at the wrist most characteristically affects:
questions.explanation: The recurrent branch of the median nerve supplies thenar muscles responsible for thumb opposition.

questions.question: The most important immediate step for a newborn who is apneic after initial drying and stimulation is:
questions.explanation: If a newborn remains apneic or has inadequate breathing after initial steps, positive-pressure ventilation is indicated.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.question: Physiologic neonatal jaundice typically appears:
questions.explanation: Jaundice appearing in the first 24 hours is considered pathologic until proven otherwise.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.question: Apgar score is routinely assessed at:
questions.explanation: Apgar scoring is commonly recorded at 1 and 5 minutes after birth, with further scoring when indicated.

questions.explanation: The ampullary portion of the fallopian tube is the most common site of tubal ectopic pregnancy.

questions.subject: Gynaecology
questions.question: A typical early presentation of ectopic pregnancy includes:
options: Amenorrhea, abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding
questions.explanation: The classic triad includes amenorrhea, abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding, although not all patients have all three.

questions.subject: Gynaecology
questions.question: A hemodynamically unstable patient with suspected ruptured ectopic pregnancy generally requires:
questions.explanation: Ruptured ectopic pregnancy with hemodynamic instability is a surgical emergency.
